title: Meadow Farm: a season of code
status: Playable design prototypes; not integrated main-game levels

chapters.title: Back to Meadow Farm
chapters.story: You inherit a quiet, overgrown farm. Learn the paths and find the old entrance before work begins.
chapters.retire: Direction arrows fade after level 3; the solution is no longer pre-filled after level 2.

chapters.title: The first market basket
chapters.story: A neighbour needs the farm’s first basket of produce. Learn to stop, face a plant, and harvest it.
chapters.retire: Step-by-step navigation prompts disappear; movement is now assumed knowledge.

chapters.title: A rhythm in the rows
chapters.story: The market order grows. Recognise repeated work rather than writing every step again.
chapters.retire: Repeated single commands give way to loop blocks; loops become a mastery goal.

chapters.title: After the storm
chapters.story: An overnight storm leaves stones across familiar lanes. Restore access before the next collection.
chapters.retire: Single-action harvest demonstrations disappear; known loop patterns remain available.

chapters.title: The dry nursery
chapters.story: Rain stops and the new carrot beds wilt. Bring the nursery back to life in the right order.
chapters.retire: Ready-to-harvest plants become supporting tasks; unlimited water avoids introducing two rules at once.

chapters.title: Water for everyone
chapters.story: The village shares a limited water supply. Use the pump and plan refills to keep every bed alive.
chapters.retire: Unlimited watering is retired explicitly; capacity starts at two and remains consistent.

progressionRules: Every fifth level is a checkpoint using only concepts taught earlier in that chapter.
A new mechanic is introduced on a familiar short route before it appears in loops or longer routes.
Previously learned controls persist. Tutorial prompts, trivial repetition and unlimited water are retired gradually.
Water is unlimited until level 26; a visible two-portion limit is introduced explicitly at the pump.
Loops are a mastery requirement on marked levels, not an assumed property of one supplied solution.
The stage labels describe support, not a promise that every second level introduces a new API.

futureExpansion.bridge: First show ripe and unripe states with a single known harvest action; introduce the condition separately.
Replace a familiar long loop body with a named care routine; do not introduce functions and parameters together.
